entities.summary: Roger de Pins was a prominent figure in the Knights Hospitaller during the 14th century, playing a crucial role in the Order's expansion and influence in the Mediterranean region. As grand master from 1355 to 1365, de Pins oversaw the Order's military campaigns and diplomatic efforts, forging alliances with European monarchs and securing key territories. His leadership and strategic thinking helped the Knights Hospitaller maintain their position as a major military and religious power in the region. De Pins' legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as the Order continued to thrive under his successors and played a significant role in shaping the course of European history. The Knights Hospitaller's extensive archives, which de Pins helped establish, remain a valuable resource for historians studying the Order's history and the medieval Mediterranean world. De Pins' own tomb in the Jerusalem Hospice, a testament to his enduring legacy, stands as a poignant reminder of his significance in the history of the Knights Hospitaller and the broader region.
